scope: Accepted 1856-1857 batch-42 source-text rendering, chronology, attribution, special-markup, figure and missing-input requirements only. Candidate documentation; no converter, transcript, export, training or accepted evidence changes.

requirements.case: 1837 rejected same-author proposal and missing Thwaites prompt
requirements.requirement: Keep Darwin’s March 8 response as a same-author continuation/proposal, not a newly identified Thwaites reply. Darwin explicitly acknowledges a missing Thwaites letter, asks for alpine/Ceylon observations and requests pigeon skins; extant Darwin letters are not Q/A substitutes. Later manuscript quotation cannot reconstruct the missing Thwaites prompt.

evidence.quote: As you have received my letter in so very friendly a spirit
You cannot possibly render me more material assistance than by getting me any skins

requirements.requirement: Preserve Darwin’s thanks for a missing Tyndall note and Huxley mediation, his ignorance of mechanics, and his proposed dry/wetted ice experiment as a proposal. Later controversy or completed cleavage results must not be inserted into this February 1857 response. The postscript remains substantive but does not identify a missing incoming text.

evidence.quote: I am very much obliged to you for your note
I am so very glad to hear that you are continuing your experiments on ice
It is beautiful your having given cleavage to ice.

requirements.case: 1953 Wallace receipt, fraction, voice and custody
requirements.requirement: Keep Wallace’s September 10 letter and its explicit September 4 receipt of Darwin’s June 22 note separate from the body’s observer reports, hearsay and custody claims. Preserve the literal rabbit weight 3 to 3½ lb as MathML, not a normalized decimal. Crab predation on chicks is witnessed while rabbit predation is inferred; cat weights include seen 15 lb and heard 20 lb. The cat is preserved but not yet shipped, goat skin/horns are intended for Lindley, and the recipient address is excluded. Preserve the substantive postscript and its undated annotations separately; do not repair the P11 missing wording.

evidence.quote: I received your note dated June 22nd. 1856 on the 4th. of this Month
Rabbits are found from the before named districts
I beleive both Guinea Fowl and Rabbits are much persecuted when young by Cats

requirements.mathml_policy: Retain source MathML half in rabbit weight; do not flatten to an inferred decimal.

requirements.case: 2078 three-cell figure and revised publication memory
requirements.requirement: Keep Waterhouse’s account as a checked but negative literature search followed by a revised suspicion that he never published the Osmia cell account. His description of the oval mud cell and the jaw-smoothing observation is distinct from later 1858/Origin explanations. Preserve the actual three contacting rounded-cell drawing with converging shared boundaries, no labels or scale; do not render it as a regular hexagonal comb. P3–P4 after the signature are substantive source text.

evidence.quote: I have now looked into them & find nothing connected
I have always laboured under the impression that I did publish an account

figure.observation: Three contacting rounded cells with straight shared boundaries converging centrally; no labels or scale.

requirements.case: 1810 eighteen XML alternatives and copyist corrections
requirements.requirement: Preserve the raw XML set of eighteen monthly-18th alternatives and the weekday constraint, leaving 18 August 1856, 18 May 1857 and 18 January 1858 all possible. Darwin’s refusal of the reviewing proposal, hypothetical £15-per-sheet valuation, and illness remain source content; Greg/Grey and soul/sould corrections stay copyist/editorial apparatus. Do not force an August date or recreate the missing offer.

evidence.quote: I am much pleased & flattered at Mr. Gregs proposal
I have so many years work in prospect in my present book on species & varieties

requirements.requirement: Keep Darwin’s April 21 [1856] response to Godfrey’s rabbit report distinct from later gamekeeper information. The report establishes only a breed running wild for some years; the postscript explicitly says bodies are not worth sending because the history is obscure. Do not convert thanks into specimen receipt or import later ancestry evidence.

evidence.quote: I fear the case has broken down, except so far as knowing that such a breed has run wild for some years
it is not worth sending the bodies

requirements.requirement: Reuse the already accepted 2070 reading only as prior evidence: Hensleigh’s etymological illustration supports a later 1857 chapter-use witness, not a new batch-42 relationship or an 1844 knowledge claim. Do not duplicate its accepted edge or infer an exact receipt date from chapter completion.

Keep headers, XML alternatives, retained body blocks, postscript position, annotations, footnotes, bibliography, nested/third-party voices, MathML and figures separate. Missing Thwaites/Tyndall/Darwin prompts, approximate reports and future experiments cannot be reconstructed from later controversies or publication outcomes. Existing accepted relationship scopes remain immutable.

validation_notes: Retained body paragraph numbers are distinct from raw DOM indexes, including salutation, opener and postscript blocks. Quotes are literal where body content is quoted; MathML and figure evidence are recorded separately. No later outcome or missing prompt is synthesized.
